results.caveats: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.
results.methodology_other: UNOSAT datasets and maps are produced using a variety of methods. In general, analysts closely review satellite imagery, often comparing two or more images together, and determine notable changes between the images. For damage assessments, refugee or IDP assessments, and similar analyses, these changes are then manually documented in the vector data by the analyst. For flood extractions, landcover mapping and similar analyses, a variety of automated remote sensing techniques are used to extract the relevant information which is then reviewed and revised as necessary by the analyst. In all cases, resulting data is then loaded into a standardized UNOSAT geodatabase and exported asshapefiles for dissemination.
results.name: evaluacion-de-danos-en-edificaciones-en-la-ciudad-de-zarzal-valle-del-cauca-colombia-al-13
results.notes:
**UNOSAT code: EQ20260810COL, GDACS ID: 1557236**  Este mapa presenta una evaluación de daños basada en imágenes satelitales de la ciudad de Zarzal, departamento Valle del Cauca, ubicada aproximadamente a 50 km del área epicentral del terremoto de magnitud 7,4 ocurrido el 10 de agosto de 2026 en Colombia.   
Los daños fueron identificados principalmente en una imágen satelital Pléiades de muy alta resolución, adquirida el 13 de agosto de 2026. Dentro del área analizada, se identificaron 21 edificaciones con daños y 180 edificaciones como potencialmente dañadas. El alto ángulo de incidencia (>40°) de las imágenes satelitales utilizadas para este análisis puede afectar la precisión de los resultados. Por lo tanto, las estimaciones de daños derivadas de imágenes satelitales con un ángulo de incidencia tan elevado deben interpretarse con precaución.  
  
Este es un análisis preliminar que aún no ha sido validado en campo. Se recomienda realizar una verificación en terreno. Los comentarios y observaciones pueden enviarse al Centro de Satélites de las Naciones Unidas.

results.caveats:
ground_truth: the footprint matches a hand-digitized damage label. damage=1
confirmed: a reviewer inspected the imagery and confirmed the building is damaged or neighboring area is damaged.  damaged = 1 .
rejected: a reviewer inspected the imagery and judged the building undamaged, i.e. a model false positive.  damaged = 0 , and all  damage_pct_*  probability fields are zeroed.
unsure: a reviewer inspected the imagery but it was inconclusive. Conservatively retains  damaged = 1  and should be excluded from high-confidence damage counts.
results.methodology_other:
Creamos evaluaciones de daños a nivel de edificio tras el terremoto en Colombia mediante el entrenamiento y la posterior ejecución de un modelo de inteligencia artificial sobre imágenes satelitales adquiridas después del desastre. El modelo de IA clasifica cada edificio identificado en las imágenes como “sin daños”, “afectado” o “desconocido”. La categoría “desconocido” se utiliza cuando el edificio no puede ser evaluado adecuadamente, por ejemplo, debido a la presencia de nubes. Utilizamos los polígonos de edificios de Overture and Google, que representan el estado de las edificaciones sobre el terreno antes del evento. Los resultados se distribuyen como un archivo vectorial en formato GeoPackage, con los siguientes atributos para cada edificio: id – identificador único de Overture para cada edificio. damaged – valor 1 si el edificio está dañado; de lo contrario, 0. unknown – valor 1 si el edificio está cubierto por nubes, neblina, humo o si, por alguna otra razón, no fue posible clasificarlo; de lo contrario, 0. area – área del edificio en metros cuadrados.

We create building level damage assessments by training and then running an AI model on the post-disaster imagery. The AI model predicts whether each footprint in the imagery is "building", "damaged", or "unknown" (i.e. cloudy). We use Google and Overture building footprints which represent the state on the ground pre-event and distribute the resulting data as a vector file GeoPackage with the following per-footprint attributes: id – the Overture Maps unique ID for each footprint damaged – 1 if the building is damaged, else 0 unknown – 1 if the building was covered by clouds/haze/smoke or otherwise unable to be classified, else 0 area – area of the building in sq meters
results.name: colombia-2026-earthquake-pereira-extended
results.notes:
Microsoft AI for Good Lab ran their damage assessment AI models over an extended area of Pereira.

Google summary: Out of a total of 152,128 building footprints with predictions in the study area, 8,656 were fully obscured by clouds. Of the remaining 143,472 non-cloudy footprints, the model predicted that 752 (0.5%) were damaged to some extent.
 
Overture summary: Out of a total of 77,589 building footprints with predictions in the study area, 6,582 were fully obscured by clouds. Of the remaining 71,007 non-cloudy footprints, the model predicted that 441 (0.6%) were damaged to some extent.
 
Microsoft summary: Out of a total of 123,924 building footprints with predictions in the study area, 7,731 were fully obscured by clouds. Of the remaining 116,193 non-cloudy footprints, the model predicted that 650 (0.6%) were damaged to some extent.

El modelo de IA clasifica cada edificio identificado en las imágenes como “sin daños”, “afectado” o “desconocido”. La categoría “desconocido” se utiliza cuando el edificio no puede ser evaluado adecuadamente, por ejemplo, debido a la presencia de nubes.
Utilizamos los polígonos de edificios de Overture Maps, que representan el estado de las edificaciones sobre el terreno antes del evento. Los resultados se distribuyen como un archivo vectorial en formato GeoPackage, con los siguientes atributos para cada edificio:
id – identificador único de Overture Maps y Google para cada edificio.
damaged – valor 1 si el edificio está dañado; de lo contrario, 0.
unknown – valor 1 si el edificio está cubierto por nubes, neblina, humo o si, por alguna otra razón, no fue posible clasificarlo; de lo contrario, 0.
area – área del edificio en metros cuadrados.

We create building level damage assessments by training and then running an AI model on the post-disaster imagery. The AI model predicts whether each footprint in the imagery is "building", "damaged", or "unknown" (i.e. cloudy). We use Overture Maps and Google building footprints which represent the state on the ground pre-event and distribute the resulting data as a vector file GeoPackage with the following per-footprint attributes: id – the Overture Maps unique ID for each footprint damaged – 1 if the building is damaged, else 0 unknown – 1 if the building was covered by clouds/haze/smoke or otherwise unable to be classified, else 0 area – area of the building in sq meters
